newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan insurers undecided on Sanyo Sec loan delay.
newsitem.headline: Japan insurers undecided on Sanyo Sec loan delay.

text.p: Two major Japanese life insurers said on Friday that they have not yet decided whether to accept a request from Sanyo Securities Co Ltd for a delay in the repayment of its subordinated loans.

The medium-sized brokerage had a total of 20 billion yen in subordinated loans from nine life insurers at the end of March, 1996, including four billion yen from Nippon Life and three billion from Dai-Ichi Mutual, a Sanyo financial report said.
Industry sources said that the insurers provided the subordinated loans in February 1995 and have already extended the repayment date twice over the past two years.
Asked if Sanyo plans to review the nine-year restructuring programme, a Sanyo spokesman said: "We do not plan to change the framework of the restructuring programme."
Under the programme, creditors agreed to cut interest rates on outstanding loans to its non-bank affiliate and Sanyo Securities pledged to help the affiliate dispose of problem loans.

The spokesman said that Sanyo has been striving to cut costs and restructure its operations to boost profits, adding that the company was confident that the request for an extension would be approved by the life insurers.
